records.issue_text: [BUG] The else-branch increments retryCount for reminders whose SMS has ALREADY been successfully scheduled, and the new deleteMany OR clause then deletes them. A reminder that scheduled successfully on a previous cron run reaches retryCount 2 on the next run's else-branch; the deleteMany `retryCount > 1` clause (lines 31-40) then removes the WorkflowReminder row, cancelling the Twilio scheduled message reference — users stop receiving valid reminders, and operators see reminders silently vanish.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch-block retryCount increment runs even when the thrown error is itself a Prisma/database failure, and the increment is not wrapped in its own error handling. When the DB is down, the prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch throws an unhandled rejection that aborts the remaining loop iterations, so no subsequent reminders in the batch are attempted on that run — the error handling makes partial-failure worse than doing nothing.
records.rationale: In the new error path, the `catch (error)` block performs `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` without its own guarding try/catch. If the original error is a Prisma/DB failure (e.g., DB down), this update will also throw, escaping the catch and aborting the loop early, preventing subsequent reminders from being processed in that run. This behavior is directly shown by the added `await prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch with no additional error handling.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write that can clobber concurrent increments and uses a stale value read before the Twilio call. Two overlapping cron invocations (the endpoint is an authenticated API route that can be triggered concurrently) both read retryCount=0, both fail, both write 1 — the reminder survives one full extra retry cycle beyond the intended limit and, conversely, a successful retry path can be overwritten by a concurrent failure path, marking a scheduled reminder for deletion.
records.rationale: The diff shows `retryCount` is read in the initial `findMany` result (`select: { ...select, retryCount: true }`) and later updated via a non-atomic read-modify-write: `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` in both the `else` branch and `catch`. Because the endpoint can be invoked concurrently, two overlapping runs can both read the same `reminder.retryCount` and write the same incremented value, losing an increment. records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block increments retryCount even for non-retryable errors, and the throwaway-update itself can throw, aborting the remaining reminders in the loop. If the prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch rejects (e.g. reminder row deleted by the deleteMany of a concurrent run), the exception escapes the loop and every subsequent unscheduled reminder in this batch is skipped until the next cron run, delaying all SMS reminders; additionally, permanent Twilio errors (invalid phone number, account suspended) burn both retries then silently delete the reminder with no operator-visible record beyond a console.log.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry mechanism depends entirely on the next cron invocation re-selecting the failed reminder, but the selection window still filters scheduledDate to <= now + 7 days, so a reminder whose scheduledDate drifts past that window is silently dropped rather than retried. A reminder that fails twice quickly (retryCount=2 is not reached because it is deleted at retryCount>1 after the second failure) is deleted; a reminder that fails once and whose scheduledDate passes before the next cron run is deleted by the first deleteMany branch — end users silently miss SMS reminders with no exhausted-retry signal to operators.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retry design permanently deletes a reminder after two failed scheduling attempts instead of dead-lettering it, so an attendee silently never receives their reminder whenever the failure is transient over multiple cron runs (e.g. a Twilio outage or expired credentials lasting >2 runs). Every SMS reminder whose scheduling failed twice is hard-deleted by the deleteMany OR retryCount > 1 branch with no notification, logging, or fallback record — the booking's attendee never gets the reminder and there is no audit trail that it was dropped; a single persistent infrastructure error permanently destroys all pending SMS reminders.
records.rationale: The diff implements hard-deletion of reminders once `retryCount > 1` via the new `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })` filter. Since `retryCount` is incremented on scheduling failure (`data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` in both the `else` branch and the `catch`), any reminder that fails twice will have `retryCount` reach 2 and will be deleted on the next cron run, with no alternate persistence/audit path shown in the diff.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount > 1 deletion branch is not scoped to method: SMS or scheduledDate, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 regardless of channel or timing, unlike the original clause which was scoped to SMS and past dates. If retryCount is ever populated by any other path (or a future worker reuses the column for other channels), those reminders are deleted while still pending; even within this diff, a reminder whose scheduledDate is in the future (within the 7-day scheduling window) is deleted on the next cron tick after its second failure, removing reminders that could still have been scheduled successfully on a later attempt.
records.rationale: The diff changes the cleanup deleteMany filter from being scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduledDate <= now` to an `OR` where the second branch is just `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no additional constraints. This will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row (any method/channel, any scheduledDate) once `retryCount > 1`. In the same diff, `retryCount` is incremented on scheduling failures, so an SMS reminder with a future `scheduledDate` that fails twice can be deleted on the next cron tick even though it is still within the scheduling window.
